name: Autosomal Dominant Hereditary Demyelinating Motor and Sensory Neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Criteria for CMT1

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Reduced motor nerve conduction velocity (<38 m/s) consistent with demyelination
Symmetric distal muscle weakness and atrophy with sensory loss predominantly in lower limbs
Identification of pathogenic mutation in PMP22, MPZ, or related genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history plus clinical features of distal motor and sensory neuropathy and electrophysiological evidence of demyelination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and electrophysiological criteria are met

pathognomonic.symptomName: Symmetric distal muscle weakness and atrophy
searchTerms: weakness and muscle loss in hands and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced motor nerve conduction velocity indicating demyelination
searchTerms: slow nerve signals in motor nerves
reduced feeling in hands and feet
loss of sensation in fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Distal lower limb hyporeflexia or areflexia
searchTerms: absent or reduced reflexes in lower legs

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop
tingling sensations in hands and feet
abnormal sensations in fingers and toes

occasional.symptomName: Foot ulcers secondary to sensory loss
searchTerms: ulcers on feet due to numbness

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal limb pain or cramps
searchTerms: mild pain or cramps in hands and feet
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Nerve conduction studies showing slowed conduction velocities consistent with demyelination
Electromyography demonstrating chronic denervation and reinnervation
imaging: MRI may show nerve hypertrophy in peripheral nerves
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in PMP22 gene duplication (most common)
Mutations in MPZ, LITAF, or EGR2 genes
other: Muscle biopsy rarely required but may show demyelination and remyelination features

distinguishingFeatures: Axonal neuropathy with normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities
Later onset and less prominent demyelination
Recurrent focal neuropathies triggered by minor trauma or compression
Usually caused by PMP22 deletion rather than duplication

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness or sensory loss
Bulbar symptoms such as dysphagia or dysarthria
references: Bird TD. Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Type 1. GeneReviews® [Internet]. 2020.
Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
